reconcile.note: John Gill resolves the son count by holding that the three sons of 2 Samuel 14:27 died young, leaving Absalom truly sonless when he raised his memorial pillar.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How many sons did Absalom have?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/absalom.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: To Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a beautiful face.
sides.verseText: To Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a beautiful face.

sides.snippet: I have no son to keep my name in memory: and he called the pillar after his own name; and it is called Absalom's monument, to this day.
sides.verseText: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar, which is in the king's dale; for he said, I have no son to keep my name in memory: and he called the pillar after his own name; and it is called Absalom's monument, to this day.
